draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Varkala town! It's called the "Varanasi of the South" because of the Janardana Swami Temple, which local lore says is about 2,000 years old. The cliffs on its coast are a National Geological Monument.
draft.hungryLine: In town, there are good places by the railway station, from cakes to all-veg meals.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Visit Sivagiri, where Sree Narayana Guru rests, then head to the Janardanaswamy Temple.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit quietly at Sivagiri hill, a peaceful pilgrim spot in the middle of town.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Varkala cliffs formed between 23 and 2.58 million years ago, through erosion.

legends.title: Where the cloth fell
legends.body: Nine prajapatis asked sage Narada how to wash away their sins. He threw his garment, the valkalam, and told them to pray where it landed, which became Varkala.

legends.title: A king's penance
legends.body: Local lore says Brahma told a Pandyan king to build a Vishnu temple to make up for his sins. He built the Janardana Swami Temple here.

tips.title: Plan around the pilgrimage.
tips.body: The Sivagiri Pilgrimage draws huge crowds from 30 December to 1 January.

tips.title: Respect temple rules.
tips.body: Non-Hindus can't enter the Janardhana temple's inner sanctum, but can look around the temple.

story.title: Cliffs from the sea
story.body: Erosion carved the Varkala cliffs between 23 and 2.58 million years ago. They now stretch 7.5 km along the coast.

story.title: The temple
story.body: Local lore says a Pandyan king built the Janardana Swami Temple here. Varkala has been a Hindu pilgrimage site since the 12th century.

story.title: The tunnel
story.body: The British built the Varkala Tunnel.

story.title: Sivagiri Matha
story.body: The Sivagiri Matha was built on Sivagiri hill. Sree Narayana Guru made Varkala his headquarters.

story.title: The Guru's resting place
story.body: Guru died here in 1928, and thousands of pilgrims still visit his samadhi every year.

food.name: Reena Bakers
